News.title: Why infants orphaned by Ebola will have to fend for themselves this time
News.content:
When Ebola tore through the Democratic Republic of Congo between 2018 and 2020, one of the few glimmers of hope to emerge from the devastation were the “lullaby mothers” – survivors who, protected by their own immunity, cared for infants orphaned by the disease.

Yet we are unlikely to see the same with the current outbreak now sweeping central Africa. It is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola and the pool of survivors from past outbreaks is much smaller.

For now, at least, there are no women with immunity who can safely enter the contamination zones to care for children and babies who have been isolated to stop the virus spreading. For the children, it will make an already terrifying experience all the more frightening.

It is also another sign of the challenge posed by the Bundibugyo variant, for which there are no approved vaccines, no proven treatments, and which has only caused two other small outbreaks before this.

“We don’t know if [people previously infected] are immune to the Bundibugyo strain of the virus,” Dr Nathalie Macdermott, a visiting professor at King’s College London, told The Telegraph.

“It would be very risky to put someone in that environment, because you may well be exposing them to Ebola again.”

News.title: How does Ebola spread, what are the symptoms, and can it be treated?
News.content:
Dr Ngashi Ngongo, professor of epidemiology and principal advisor of programmes management at Africa CDC, said it was too early to discern how fast the disease was spreading.

“Once we get good surveillance data, we can then see the rate at which cases are increasing,” he said. “The surveillance system is still weak, the contact tracing is still very weak”.

Two cases have also been reported in Uganda’s capital, Kampala, with one death. Both had travelled from the DRC. There has not yet been any suspected onward spread in the country.

Uganda on Sunday postponed next month’s celebrations for Martyrs’ Day, ⁠a national ​holiday that usually draws thousands of pilgrims from eastern DRC, because of the outbreak.

Neighbouring countries have expressed concern about the possibility of further cross-border spread.

Dr Menelas Nkeshimana, Head of the Health Workforce Development Department at Rwanda’s Ministry of Health, who was on the frontlines of the country’s Marburg outbreak, said haemorrhagic fever epidemics should be detected and contained much earlier.

“Strong early detection benefits not only the affected country, but also protects neighbouring nations and the broader region,” he told The Telegraph.

When did the outbreak start?

It is not clear exactly when the current outbreak began – a fact that poses challenges for the response.

Health officials in the DRC are working on the assumption that the virus began spreading in mid-April, but the first confirmed case was not reported until May 14.

Two days later, there were eight confirmed cases, 246 suspected cases and 80 suspected deaths, according to the CDC.

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO director general, on Friday said the global health body first learned of suspected cases on May 5 and dispatched ​a team to Ituri, but samples ​collected in the field initially tested ⁠negative.

Jean Pierre Badombo, the former mayor of Mongbwalu, a mining town in Ituri, said people started falling ill in mid-April after a large open-casket funeral procession arrived from Bunia, the regional capital.

“After that, we experienced a cascade of deaths,” he said.

Is there a vaccine?

While a vaccine for the Zaire strain has been in use since 2019, there is currently no approved vaccine for the Bundibugyo variant, nor are there any vaccine candidates in late-stage clinical development that could be readily deployed to fight the outbreak.

As a result, the response effort is largely relying on classical public health control measures and supportive clinical care, said Dr Daniela Manno, Clinical Assistant Professor at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine.

These measures include isolating the infected, contact tracing, and enforcing infection prevention and control for health workers.

Four experimental treatments are under consideration for use against the outbreak, according to the Africa CDC. These include remdesivir, the antiviral drug widely used during the Covid-19 pandemic, and a monoclonal antibody therapy called DP134.

Officials said discussions were underway with the authorities in Uganda and the DRC to deploy the therapeutics under randomised controlled trial protocols, although none of the studies had yet begun.

What threat does it pose to the rest of the world?

The WHO has already declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) – a step only taken eight times before now – after cases were reported in Uganda.

Experts say the outbreak poses a threat to the African continent, especially if cases are confirmed in neighbouring countries in the following days.

Jeremy Konyndyk, president of Refugees International and a former senior adviser to USAID, said the outbreak was “already dramatically bigger” than the 2014 to 2016 West African Ebola epidemic at a comparable stage.

“That is just astonishing and makes me quite nervous,” he said.

News.title: DRC’s Ebola outbreak could be twice as large as reported
News.content:
The Ebola outbreak in central Africa could be twice as big as currently reported, according to a study published by Imperial College London.

On Wednesday, the World Health Organization (WHO) said there were nearly 600 suspected cases and 179 deaths in the outbreak that is sweeping hard-to-reach areas of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s north east.

However, a study published by the MRC Centre for Global Infectious Disease Analysis, part of Imperial, suggests there could be up to 1,700 cases in a worst-case scenario.

The central estimate for the study, which used two different methods of calculating the scale of the outbreak, was lower, at between 400 to 800 cases.

“Both methods yield broadly consistent results, suggesting that as of 17 May 2026, approximately 400 to 800 cases of BVD may have occurred in the Democratic Republic of the Congo,” say the authors, who include Prof Neil Ferguson, the epidemiologist whose research helped shape the UK response to Covid-19 in 2020.

“However, there is considerable uncertainty around these estimates, with values of over 1,000 not being able to be excluded given current data,” they add.

News.title: How measles unleashed a wave of suffering in Bangladesh
News.content:
Delirious with lingering fever after contracting measles a fortnight ago, one-year-old Yusuf could soon die from a disease he should be protected against.

Propped up by his mother Nafisa on a temporary intensive care bed so she can keep the nebuliser over his mouth, the tiny boy is one of thousands of Bangladeshi children struck down by the worst global measles outbreak in years.

For now, an IV drip and oxygen sustain his fragile, listless frame. But Yusuf – whose eyes have been bandaged over to help him sleep – has a bleak prognosis.

The measles ward at the DNCC repurposed Covid-19 Hospital in Dhaka Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

It is, sadly, a common one in a country currently overwhelmed by measles.

An immunisation gap caused mainly by the overthrow of Bangladesh’s authoritarian government in 2024 provided the catalyst for an unprecedented surge in cases which has so far claimed at least 424 lives.

A tiny measles patient Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

More than 55,000 infections have been recorded since mid-March, according to the country’s Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), and hospital wards are over capacity with critically ill children.

Most of the victims of the epidemic are under 10, with the highest concentration among under-fives. Last week, 11 children died from measles in less than 24 hours.

Over the course of a week in Bangladesh, I witnessed the harrowing suffering unleashed when a whole nation’s vaccine distribution infrastructure is disrupted by bureaucratic collapse.

Six-month-old Mizanur Rahman on a measles overflow ward Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

For places where vaccine hesitancy has led to smaller recent outbreaks, including in London and Birmingham, it provides a blunt reminder of measles’ potential seriousness.

In Bangladesh, until recently praised by the World Health Organization (WHO) for its immunisation coverage, the mortality rate among children infected with the virus is high because of complications linked to malnourishment and pneumonia.

The ward in which I find Yusuf is in a former shopping mall converted into a makeshift hospital during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Rarely used since, except during a seasonal uptick in dengue fever cases, the Dhaka North City Corporation hospital is managed by the Bangladeshi military. It was repurposed for measles when the sprawling city’s Infectious Disease Hospital could no longer cope.

Eerily empty walkways between wards are lined with shuttered shop units.

Our escort, a uniformed army officer, tells me that in less than six weeks they have admitted more than 3,000 measles patients.

The DNCC Covid-19 Hospital, in a former shopping complex, has been repurposed to deal with the measles outbreak Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

“I was here during Covid and the dengue crisis in 2023,” says nurse Nazma Khan, 40. “This feels more severe because all of the patients are children. It is pitiful to see them in such a condition. They cannot express their suffering.”

As with many on the intensive care ward, Yusuf, from Shariatpur, three hours outside the capital, is not receiving the treatment he needs as medical fees are too expensive for his family.

“Doctors have told me that his brain has probably been affected by the measles infection,” says terrified Nafisa, 22. “Every time I turn away, he seems to get worse. He has been in a daze for so many days now. His eyes cannot focus anymore; he can’t really eat or sleep.

“He missed the measles vaccine, which he should have got when he was nine months old. Now he is so desperately ill. I feel helpless. The treatment he requires we can only get at a private clinic, but that would cost us twice what my husband earns in a whole month, for just a single day.”

Hospital wards are over capacity with critically ill children Credit : Simon Townsley

The disparity between the healthcare haves and have-nots is underlined by a flicker of movement that catches my eye next to Yusuf’s bed, a tiny cockroach scampering across the floor. On our way in, I was shown a dedicated private intensive care room for VIP patients.

At a nearby bed, exhausted parents Abdur Rajjak, 34, and wife Joynab, 33, are struggling to cope with having three of their four children, aged eight, five and one, in the hospital with measles. Their five-year-old, Obaidulah, is being kept separately in an isolation ward.

“All of my children missed their measles vaccinations,” admits Abdur. “I regret it so much. Normally, we would not be here. We are the most concerned about our son. He is in a very severe condition.

Paediatric Consultant Faria Yasmin examines an x-ray with a colleague on the Measles Intensive Care Ward Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

“Neither me nor my wife have really slept properly for ten days. It’s just the two of us. Our relatives are scared to come in because they don’t want to risk catching measles.”

As I walk around the ward, I am accosted by dozens of fearful parents. All seem equally shocked to be in this predicament so soon after what started out as a runny nose and high temperature.

It is noisy and chaotic. I quickly become inured to the unceasing background noise of rasping coughs, high-pitched wails and groans.

The highest concentration of measles patients is among the under-fives Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

One exhausted mother is asleep on a mattress that has briefly been vacated by a patient, before being rudely awakened for a new arrival.

Plastic bags stuffed with cough syrups and calamine lotion are scattered across the tiled floor. Some families eat rice and lentils from metal pots. Sanitation seems unavoidably ad-hoc.

Paediatric consultant Dr Faria Yasnim tells me there has been an “exponential increase” since children first arrived with measles rashes, the majority aged six to eight months.

“Usually, we would expect them to be protected by maternal antibodies passed on through breastfeeding,” she explains. “However, many of these babies’ mothers have also missed their vaccine, or they were too weak to breastfeed because of their poor diet. It is a scenario none of us have encountered before. Nearly all of the patients are critical and need oxygen.

“Often it is too late by the time they get here. The gap between infection and detection is too long.”

A mother lies next to her sick child on the measles intensive care ward Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Bangladesh’s deadly measles outbreak this year is extreme, but several other countries have also experienced recent surges that run contrary to the overall global downward trend towards elimination through herd immunity.

Dozens of children have died from measles in Yemen, the majority unvaccinated. Last year there were 214 deaths from the disease in the war-ravaged country.

In Pakistan, 71 paediatric deaths due to measles were recorded in the first four months of 2026. Health authorities there say the spike is driven by a backlog of children who missed routine vaccinations during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Mexico is also undergoing an untimely acceleration in measles infection, which has triggered alarm ahead of the World Cup next month.

Dhaka’s population density makes it an ideal breeding ground for a highly contagious airborne virus spread by coughs and sneezes Credit : Simon Townsley

In the US, which is hosting the most games including all of England and Scotland’s group stage fixtures, WHO measles elimination status achieved 26 years ago is under threat from persistent outbreaks often triggered by anti-vaccine misinformation.

Eighty-five per cent of people infected in Utah this year had not received the standard two doses of the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine.

A train passes through downtown Dhaka Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Japan, granted measles elimination status in 2015, has also weathered a spike centred around Tokyo. Health authorities there suspect the virus might have been imported by foreign tourists.

Whereas the mortality rate from measles is approximately 1 in 5,000 in the UK, in Bangladesh there are around seven deaths for every 1,000 recorded cases during the ongoing outbreak.

Bangladesh is the only country in the world ranking in the top 10 for both population density and total population, making it ideal breeding ground for a highly contagious airborne virus spread by coughs and sneezes.

Until the uprising that toppled despotic former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh prided itself on its strong childhood vaccination programme.

According to the British Medical Journal (BMJ), the country maintained between 90 per cent and 95 per cent MMR coverage up to 2025, aside from an understandable dip during the Covid pandemic.

A defaced mural of Sheikh Hasina Wazed, Bangladesh’s reviled former Prime Minister, who is blamed for many of the current issues facing the country. Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

During the period of the interim government from August 2024 to February 2026, however, the mass measles vaccination campaign which normally happens every four years was missed. The last one was in 2020.

Stockpiles of vaccines became depleted as the procurement process slowed down and tens of thousands of health worker roles were left vacant.

Lacking foresight, the stand-in administration failed to react quickly enough to measles outbreaks in other countries in 2024. Another factor was that data from the private hospitals which many people in Dhaka use was not collated, the BMJ report found. It was the perfect storm.

Dhaka is perhaps better known for its dengue outbreaks Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Mike Tildesley, Professor of Infectious Disease Modelling at the University of Warwick, said the difficulty facing nations with vaccination coverage problems is that the reproduction number for measles is extremely high.

As a result, herd immunity as defined by the WHO is only achieved when around 95 per cent have received the MMR jab.

“The consequence of this is that vaccination coverage doesn't need to fall very much for us to observe measles outbreaks again,” Professor Tildesley explained. “We've even seen this in the UK over the last few years, that measles cases have started to increase as a result of a drop in uptake of the MMR vaccine.”

A bus station in Dhaka Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Bangladesh’s new government is now playing catch-up with an emergency nationwide vaccination drive underway. Over four million children have already been reached.

It is a race against the clock to prevent already weakened children from dying or suffering long-term complications, including inflammation of the brain and blindness.

At the Shishu Children’s Hospital in Dhaka, ICU staff on the hastily designated Measles ICU Ward have become accustomed to the grim spectacle of grieving parents carrying their tiny children’s bodies out, shrouded in white muslin cloth.

On one bed, garment factory worker Sheuli Akhter, 24, hugs her sleeping five-year-old niece Jammatal tightly, as if to shield her from encroaching danger.

Sheulii Akhter hugs her niece Jammatal in the measles intensive care ward Credit : Simon Townsley

The two gaunt, immobile babies on the beds behind are the worst cases I have seen. I struggle to imagine them lasting long.

In the southern town of Noakhali, serious cases are being treated in a disused office building next to the main government hospital. The emergency add-on space is over capacity, with gurneys lining the corridors.

Here, most measles patients are the children of smallholding farmers, fishermen, factory workers and labourers. Many arrived in the back of a rickshaw in their parents’ arms.

Nafiza Akhter watches over her seriously ill son, Yousuf Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Their tiny throats strain with hoarse coughs, their eyes are unfocused, they are floppy, and their weakened bodies are covered with a rash that in many cases has also spread internally.

Crouching next to her prone five-month-old daughter, Maisha on another bed is 29-year-old Nazmum Nahar, her face etched by fatigue and worry.

“When we brought her here her body had turned blue,” explains Nazmum. “I thought she was going to die.”

Mohammed Akbar comforts his six-month-old son Abdul Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Although slightly improved, Maisha remains at high risk. She is desperately underweight, having arrived at hospital in an already debilitated condition.

Her recovery has been inhibited by the fact that her own recent birth was not straightforward, resulting in a hefty hospital bill for a Caesarean delivery.

“We had to hand over all the money we had when she was born,” continues her mother. “That means we cannot even afford transport for her to be transferred to a better hospital.”

For some, the vaccination campaign backed by global vaccine alliance GAVI, UNICEF and the WHO has come too late.

Moyna Khanam lost her 18-month-old daughter, Jerin, to measles at the end of March. Jerin’s was one of the first registered deaths of the virus’s resurgence. She should have received her vaccine, but the local clinic was out of stock when her mother took her in last year.

Grief-stricken Moyna with her surviving daughter, Sara Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Today, Moyna remains completely inconsolable, suffocated by raw grief. Her body shudders as she weeps, clutching her daughter’s favourite cuddly toy to her chest. Weeks have gone by, but she remains unable to process how her healthy, bubbly little girl was so swiftly snatched from her grasp.

I meet Moyna in the squalid, cobwebbed single room she lives in with her husband Tariqul Sabuj, 29, a plumber, and their elder daughter Sara, eight.

A photograph of Moyna Khanam with her 18-month-old daughter Jerin Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

Tariqul empties out a plastic bin liner containing all of Jerin’s clothing, shoes and scant toys. They sit together on the mattress in which they all sleep, sifting through mementoes of her cruelly short life.

Their cell-like concrete dwelling, which has two tiny, barred windows, is at the end of a dank, musty alley in a warren of decrepit housing blocks patrolled by stray dogs and rats. Sinks and toilets are shared between dozens of families. A hothouse for viruses.

Moyna is incandescent with rage as she berates the authorities she blames for Jerin’s awful death. Her words are muddled. She repeats the same phrase over and over like a mantra: “Why not me?”

Between stifled sobs, she musters the courage to explain her anguish. Tariqul is quietly resolute in the corner. Sara is mute and distracted.

Wasim Hawlader holds a picture of his 10-month-old son, who died after contracting measles Credit : Simon Townsley/The Telegraph

“Without Jerin this place feels completely empty,” Moyna admits. “I felt like she would be my companion for my whole life. We had such an emotional bond. She had so much energy, so much life to give.

“Now I just feel breathless all the time, like I am being crushed, and all that I can think about is the memory of when I was pregnant with her.”

“I refuse to accept she has left us,” she adds.

So many quiet tragedies are being absorbed into the frenetic chaos of Dhaka as the measles outbreak presses inexorably against its never-ending traffic.

Wasim and Ulfa at Mohammed’s grave with their surviving child Aysha Credit : Simon Townsley

Peculiarly for such a rowdy city, the cemetery in which 10-month-old Mohammed Yasin was buried at the end of March exists in an exclusive oasis of calm.

Amid rows of tiny mounds of red soil and stones already overgrown with weeds from recent heavy rainfall, I leave Mohammed’s numbed parents, father Wasim, 30, and mother Ulfa, 25, with their surviving child Aysha, three.

Freshly dug plots are the final resting place of infant measles patients.

In this beautiful, verdant spot, more like a public garden than a graveyard, sentry-still Ulfa prays silently, a potent symbol of the very real danger of neglecting the vaccine.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

Sports.title: Emotional Prince William pays bizarre tribute to Aston Villa forgotten man who didn’t even play in Europa League triumph
Sports.content:
PRINCE WILLIAM rushed onto social media to celebrate Aston Villa’s Europa League glory – and reserved special praise for a star who was ruled out of the showdown through injury.

Wills, 43, jetted out to Istanbul to watch the Midlands giants end their 44-year wait for continental silverware by thumping Freiburg 3-0.





And the Villa-mad royal was spotted getting emotional before jumping at the chance to hold the Europa League trophy with chief Unai Emery.

The Prince then headed onto X to send congratulations to his heroes after a memorable night in the club’s history.

He bizarrely paid tribute to midfielder Boubacar Kamara, who has been out of action since January.

In the social media post, William wrote: “Amazing night!! Huge congratulations to all the players, team, staff and everyone connected to the club! Forty-four years since the last taste of European silverware!

“Special shout out to Boubacar Kamara who has been out injured but is such an integral part of our team and helped lay the foundations of this success.”

Kamara, 26, has not been involved since suffering a worrying knee injury in Villa’s FA Cup third round win at Tottenham.

But the Villans still managed to get themselves over the line in the midfielder’s absence.

Villa put themselves in the box seat to add to their trophy cabinet after screamers from Youri Tielemans and Emiliano Buendia late in the first half.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And Morgan Rogers ended Freiburg’s hopes of mounting a stunning comeback by adding his name to the scoresheet after the break.

It came after the Prince shared a passionate good luck message on Instagram before the clash got underway in Turkey.

He was seen punching the air in delight after each of Villa’s strikes as he cheered them on to victory.

William started supporting the newly-crowned Europa League winners during his school days.



With most of his classmates supporting sides challenging for regular honours, he wanted to stand out from the crowd and back a side that would take him through the emotions.

And he can now expect another chance to watch his beloved club in the Champions League next season, having sealed qualification by seeing off Freiburg.

Sports.title: Harry Kane gives fans chance to win his worn Golden Boots this summer at Toca Social
Sports.content:
HARRY KANE has unveiled his very own golden boot – which he has worn – that one lucky fan will be able to take home this summer and crown themselves England’s next top striker.

To stake their claim for the trophy, players will need to complete the ‘England Challenge’ at TOCA Social.





It’s a new target-practice styled game launching that has 15 levels where the target gets progressively smaller, meaning Kane’s golden boot will only be coming home to a true sharp-shooter.

Given Kane is England‘s record goalscorer and the World Cup is looming, it does seem fitting!

Kane said: “I’m excited to give you guys the chance to win the TOCA trophy made from a pair of my own boots.

“To get your hands on them, you’ll need to get to any UK TOCA Social venue and take on the England challenge.

“It’s all about competing and having fun with your friends or family. Get down there, show us what you’ve got, and good luck!”

With 58 goals in 50 games for Bayern Munich this season, there’are nobodys noots you’d rather win right now!

Alex Harman, President of TOCA Social, believes the trophy is an extra incentive for fans to come to visit them and hopefully, watch Kane and England at the World Cup this summer.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



“As England’s greatest ever goalscorer, Harry Kane is the perfect person to launch our England Challenge and help us find another lethal finisher”

“The TOCA Trophy is an incredible prize for one fan, but it is also an invitation for everyone to lace up their shooting boots and get involved in the World Cup action.

“TOCA Social is the only venue where fans can watch the game on screen and then step up to play for themselves.”

Fans can book a private screening area for up to 30 people with gameplay before kick-off during the World Cup.

Kane is a major investor and stakeholder in TOCA Social which now has three venues; two in London and one in Birmingham.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez jumps into crowd before breaking down in tears as wild Aston Villa party erupts after Europa League victory
Sports.content:
EMI MARTINEZ could not control his joy at the end of Aston Villa’s 3-0 Europa League final triumph over Freiburg.

The Argentine goalkeeper broke down in tears at the final whistle as he dropped to his knees with his head in his hands on the floor.





As the jubilant scenes set in, Martinez erupted with emotion and joined the euphoric Villa fans in the stands.

As you’d imagine, fellow team-mates were all overjoyed on the pitch as the Midland club secured their spot in the Champions League next season.



Martinez has now been with the club for six years and this is the first honour he has secured in his tenure.

For Martinez, his emotion is quite understandable.

At the end of last season, the 33-year-old was in floods of tears believing he had played his final game for the club amid claims he was going to move on in the summer.

Of course, he ended up staying and has now played his part in leading Villa to European glory for the first time since the 1980s.



Unai Emery‘s men put in a dominant display to secure the trophy in Istanbul.

Youri Tielemans scored a wonderfully worked volley to open the scoring after around 40 minutes and Villa never looked back.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Brimming with confidence, Emi Buendia then scored a world-class left-footed curler into the top corner with the last kick of the half.

Morgan Rogers then wrapped up the victory with a goal just before the hour as their German foes never really looked like getting back into the game.

Sports.title: Man Utd star Casemiro edges closer to shock transfer with ‘verbal terms already finalised’ after heart-breaking exit
Sports.content:
CASEMIRO is reportedly closing in on a shock transfer after he leaves Manchester United.

The Brazilian midfielder has already confirmed he will make his Old Trafford exit at the end of the season.





Casemiro, 34, has recaptured his best form in recent months, which has helped the Red Devils qualify for the Champions League next term.

Despite his renewed importance to the team, his decision has remained the same and that is to seek pastures new.

talkSPORT have claimed that the former Real Madrid star is closing in on a switch across the Atlantic Ocean.

Lionel Messi‘s Inter Miami are said to have almost finalised verbal terms with Casemiro.

READ MORE ON FOOTBALL GUNNER PARTY Inside story of Arsenal stars' title party all-nighter at swanky London club

The midfielder was earning £350,000 a week during his time at United.

However, the Herons will have to navigate the deal through the MLS‘ tough financial rules.

LA Galaxy have the discovery rights on the five-time Champions League winner.

The rights are designed to stop multiple clubs in the USA from trying to sign the same player.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But any club able to pull off the financial ability to progress with the deal can do so.

Casemiro can sign a pre-contract agreement with any club overseas, but a move to Miami seems the most likely.

Should he complete the move, then he would become team-mates with his former Barcelona rival Messi.

Saudi Pro League side Al-Ittihad are also interested as they look for a replacement for former Liverpool star Fabinho.



The Brazilian is out of contract this summer after three years with the club.

Casemiro made the move to Old Trafford in a £60million deal from Real Madrid in 2022.

He has since made 160 appearances for the club and wo the FA Cup and League Cup.

Since the appointment of Michael Carrick as interim boss in January, he has been in the starting XI for every game when fit.

Sports.title: Aston Villa fans joke ‘TNT Sports can’t cope with us winning’ as TV channel CRASHES during trophy presentation
Sports.content:
TNT SPORTS 1 has gone down during its post-match coverage of Aston Villa’s Europa League triumph.

The Villans defeated Freiburg 3-0 in the Europa final to secure their first major European trophy in over 40 years.





But fans watching from home were not able to finish taking the scenes in before the broadcast went down.

The team were presented with the iconic trophy, and had their big moment broadcast as captain John McGinn held it aloft in front of the travelling fans in Istanbul.

But as the players settled down to pose and take pictures with the silverware, the broadcast cut out.

Instead of the celebrations both on the pitch and in the stands, fans watching at home were presented with only a blank blue screen.



Villa fans were both frustrated and amused at the bizarre scenes.

One fan wrote on social media: “TNT SPORTS CANT COPE WITH US WINNING.”

But other fans were less pleased, with another fan adding: “TNT sports coverage is beyond shocking.”

A third fan chimed in: “Can’t even get good coverage even if you had paid for a TNT Sports package absolute disgrace tntsports!!!!”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

And a fourth joked: “Maybe the screen has gone blue, because TNT Sports are trying to have a permanent feed on ‘prince’ William instead…”

The royal heir is a massive Villa fan and was regularly shown on the broadcast wildly celebrating his side’s goals.

Despite the broadcast interruption, for fans like him, the night will be one that lives long in the memory.

Youri Tielemans opened the scoring with an absolute stunner on the volley with five minutes of the first half left to play.



Not content to be outdone, his team-mate Emi Buendia curled home a stunner of his own from almost 30 yards in the third minute of added time in the first period, to make it 2-0 heading into the break.

Morgan Rogers then capped it off with a close-range finish twelve minutes into the second half to seal the trophy for the West Midlands side.

Sports.title: What do Bournemouth need to qualify for the Champions League on the final day of the season?
Sports.content:
WORD OF MOUTH What do Bournemouth need to qualify for the Champions League on the final day of the season?

BOURNEMOUTH will have the chance to qualify for the Champions League on the final day – but need results to go their way.

Aston Villa’s historic Europa League victory over Freiburg has opened the door to some final day drama in the Premier League.





Villa qualified for the Champions League with victory, and Liverpool are currently occupying the final Premier League qualifying spot.

Unfortunately for Xabi Alonso, he will not be managing Chelsea in the Champions League in his first season at Stamford Bridge, as the Blues cannot make it.

Brighton are also still in with an outside chance of qualifying for the European elite next season.

SunSport can reveal how Bournemouth can still qualify for the Champions League on the final day.

What do Bournemouth need to qualify for the Champions League on the final day?

Bournemouth need a handful of results to go their way, including their own.

Firstly, they will need at least a point to guarantee they finish above Brighton, as the Seagulls’ goal difference is +5 better prior to the final day.

Bournemouth sit three points ahead of them, and have a clash with Nottingham Forest at the City Ground.

They will also need two results, involving Aston Villa and Liverpool, to go their way.



Aston Villa won the Europa League on Wednesday night, meaning if they finish fifth, the Premier League will not have the five Champions League qualifiers through their coefficient ranking.

Villa qualified with the Europa League victory.

Bournemouth need Villa to lose away at Man City and fall to fifth, and for Liverpool to beat Brentford at Anfield and climb to fourth.

However, Bournemouth could also make it on points difference, if they can beat Forest and Brentford beat Liverpool, with a six-goal swing in their favour.

Brighton can also just about still make it, provided Bournemouth lose, they win at United, and the other two top five results go their way.

Sports.title: EFL statement in full as Southampton expelled from Championship play-off final over Spygate and handed points deduction
Sports.content:
SOUTHAMPTON’S appeal against their expulsion from the Championship play-off final has been DISMISSED.

The Saints made a last-ditch attempt to challenge the EFL‘s decision to throw them out of the richest game in football following ‘spygate’.





The club was found guilty of recording Middlesbrough‘s training session ahead of their Playoff semi-final showdown and two further incidents with Oxford and Ipswich have come to light.

EFL Regulation 127 prohibits any club from observing, or attempting to observe, another club’s training session within 72 hours of a scheduled match between the two clubs.

The EFL have now released a statement explaining why they will uphold their decision against Southampton.

“A League Arbitration Panel has tonight dismissed Southampton Football Club’s appeal against the Independent Disciplinary Commission’s sanction following the admittance of multiple breaches of EFL Regulations.

“The determination means that the original sanction of expulsion from the Sky Bet Championship Play -Offs remains in place, as does the four -point deduction to be applied to the 2026/27 Championship table and the reprimand in respect of all charges.

“The Club submitted its appeal following yesterday’s decision of the Independent Disciplinary Commission in respect of breaches of EFL Regulations. As per EFL Regulations, the decision of the League Arbitration Panel is final and cannot be appealed.

“Following the conclusion of the proceedings, the Sky Bet Championship Play -Off Final between Hull City and Middlesbrough is confirmed as taking place at Wembley Stadium on Saturday 23 May, kicking off at 3:30pm.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



“The League Arbitration Panel’s written reasons will be published in due course along with the Independent Disciplinary Commission’s full decision.”

The decision means Middlesbrough will indeed take their place in the Play-off final this Sunday at Wembley.

Hull City had consulted with lawyers to explore if they could automatically be promoted to the Premier League and avoid playing the Play-off final in light of Southampton’s transgressions, but the game is now definitely set.

The other thing this means is Southampton’s four-point deduction for next season also stands.

Sports.title: Freiburg 0 Aston Villa 3: Emery wins FIFTH Europa League as Prince William goes wild at Buendia and Tielemans screamers
Sports.content:
IT TAKES some serious bravery to stage a goal of the season competition in a European final.

But Youri Tielemans and Emiliano Buendia disregarded the stage and delivered two staggering show-stoppers and history for Aston Villa.





Morgan Rogers darted to the front post to add a third special strike. Unai Emery has five Europa League titles, but has never claimed one as easily as this.

A first trophy for three decades, a first European title for 44-years. Generations of Villa fans who have not witness true glory now have their own Rotterdam, three new names to place alongside Peter Withe.

And Emery has the new era he craved. I am no Europa League King he declared on the eve of this final. Pfft.

Villa staffers should be plotting his statue, Uefa considering renaming the trophy.

Istanbul, now christened Astonbul by the boys from Brum, delivered his record-extending title in this competition – in front of the future King, Prince William, himself born just after Dennis Mortimer lifted the European Cup.

Emiliano Martinez said Villa deserved this title, but they still had to grab it.



Those who have been here so long – six of the starting XI were involved in Emery’s first game in charge – are now heroes in their own right.

John McGinn would have been forever loved regardless, but now has his medal to show for it. From promotion to survival and now immortality in the claret and blue quarter of Birmingham.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

This ancient city was mobbed by Villains. 10,000 were supposed to be inside Besiktas Park, but far more had flown over and they easily outnumbered Freiburg in the stands.

Their boys were always heavy favourites, but you still have to stand up. Emery called for respect for their opponents. They showed respect and a ruthless streak.

Villa started well, Tielemans setting Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins forward after just three minutes – the former drawing an early save before bending another effort wide.



But Freiburg, playing their first-ever European final, were out to frustrate. For a while at least, it was working.

Emi Buendia and Matty Cash both found their way into the book inside just 21 minutes for fouls in their own area.

Villa could not get a grip, nor maintain rhythm. Chances were rushed and Freiburg had moments of their own. Nicolas Hofler hooked wide after Villa failed to clear a free-kick, a let off, before Martinez stopped from Johan Manzambi.

Villa nearly had another Nigel Spink moment here, with Martinez hurting his hand in the warm-up – though he was able to continue.

Emery’s side needed something to break the frustration and lift their tails – and it came from the boot of Tielemans and the mind of set-piece coach Austin MacPhee.



Villa had been warned of Freiburg’s dead-ball danger, but the Germans would never have seen this one coming.

Lucas Dinge went short to Rogers, who floated a cross well away from the pack surrounding the keeper, dropping for Tielemans just inside the box to rifle home with sublime precision.

Martinez raced from his goal to mob MacPhee, along with the substitutes.



Buendia looked the most confident of the Villa players all night and clearly would not stand for being upstaged by his Belgian teammate.

With seconds to go until the break he found space on the edge of the area, collected on the turn from McGinn and whipped and wonderstrike into the far corner in front of the Freiburg end, who fell flat.

Opposite them, delirium. The manager would tell his players they were not there yet – those in the stands were celebrating already.



Banners were out, flags were waving and tops were off. Party time.

Buendia did not want the show to stop, attempting a lob from just inside the area shortly after the restart.

Any who were left with a sick feeling in the stomach joined those already in raptures when Rogers added the third.



It was not as spectacular like the first two, but brilliant all the same. Digne fed Buendia down the left, the No10 stopping, stepping over and drilling to the front post where Watkins had dropped away and Rogers rushed forward, ahead of his man and into the history books.

They wanted more, Amadou Onana – not fit to start – was sent on and headed against the post.

Buendia wriggled free but found the side-netting – thousands thinking there was a fourth.



But three, and two all-timers, were more than enough for Emery.

The Spaniard would never have imagined the season, which started so poorly, would end like this. He revealed his deep concern at how the early weeks of this campaign had played out ahead of this final.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Way back in late September, his beloved tournament delivered a much-needed first win of the season – and now it will define it forevermore.

Villa are back in the Champions League, a staggering achievement. But nothing beats glory, nothing beats silverware.

Sports.title: Spygate LIVE: Southampton lose appeal as Middlesbrough replace them in play-off final
Sports.content:
Southampton will miss out on the play-off final after losing their appeal over the severity of the punishment dished out to them after admitting their guilt in the Spygate case

Southampton have lost their appeal, and with it their chances of making it into the play-off final to face Hull City are over. The Saints defeated Middlesbrough in the competition's semi-final but were expelled from the process after being found guilty of spying on their opponents.

Boro will now face Hull in Saturday's Championship play-off final, taking place at an earlier time of 3:30pm, after Kim Hellberg's side replaced Saints. Southampton were kicked out after they were found to have been in breach of EFL rules and also handed a four-point deduction for next season.

But the saga may not be over there. Hull could yet argue they have grounds for a case given they have had to alter their preparations for the play-off final.

The club's owner, Acun Ilicali, has given an interview confirming discussions have taken place with lawyers who have suggested they may be entitled to automatic promotion. Perhaps there will be more to come.

Sports.title: Four players who could play their final Arsenal league match against Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Four players who could play their final Arsenal league match against Crystal Palace

Arsenal will travel to Crystal Palace for the last game of this Premier League season possibly marking some players' final top-flight match for the club

View 5 Images Arsenal will travel to Crystal Palace for their final Premier League game of the season (Image: Getty)

Arsenal will bring their Premier League campaign to a close away to Crystal Palace on Sunday. But for some, it could be the last time they play for the club in the top-flight.

‌



The Gunners still have a Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain to contest after a visit to Selhurst Park as they look to win the competition for the very first time. However, some of Mikel Arteta's current squad may be sold when the next transfer window arrives.

‌



Christian Norgaard has struggled this season, having only signed in the summer of 2025 from Brentford. He has been left out of the last two Premier League matchday squads and may not feature on Sunday ahead of a premature departure. Ben White has also been linked with a move away from the Emirates, but is sidelined for the Palace clash.

‌



Yet some of Arteta's cohort might make a last league appearance before a potential exit and Mirror Football takes a look at four names in particular.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mikel Arteta's instant reaction to Pep Guardiola quitting Man City as Arsenal boss quizzed READ MORE :

Gabriel Jesus

With both Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz now seemingly ahead of Gabriel Jesus in the Arsenal striker pecking order, the Brazilian could seek pastures new this summer.

‌



View 5 Images Jesus has just over a year left on his current deal (Image: Getty)

Jesus signed a five-year deal when he arrived from Manchester City in 2022 and there has seemingly been no progress on an extension. This means his contract will expire, as things stand, in 2027.

The forthcoming window may therefore be the last time Arsenal can garner a fee for the 29-year-old, who is currently one of their highest-paid players. Although he didn't feature in their latest win against Burnley, he was on the bench and can play against Palace.

‌



Leandro Trossard

Trossard, who has scored a handful of crucial goals for the Gunners of late, could find himself in a similar situation to Jesus. He is 31 and his contract is up in 2027.

Arsenal did show faith in Trossard at the beginning of the season by upping his wages, but if a suitable offer arrives in the summer, they may cash in.

View 5 Images Trossard turns 32 this year (Image: Getty)

‌



Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke's arrivals ramped up speculation that he can leave the club and the Palace match might be the final time fans see him in the English top flight. It must be said that the Belgian has previously rubbished these rumours.

Myles Lewis-Skelly

Less likely to leave than Jesus and Trossard, Myles Lewis-Skelly has failed to secure consistent game time at Arsenal this season. He has started just four league matches.

View 5 Images Lewis-Skelly's playing time has been limited this season (Image: Getty)

‌



The 19-year-old enjoyed a stellar 2025, making his England debut and firmly entering Arteta's first-team calculations. But with Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie signed, his minutes have been greatly reduced. The Palace match may be his final league outing in Arsenal red.

If the club were to sell Lewis-Skelly, any fee generated would be pure profit and might be invested directly elsewhere. The BBC has reported that both he and fellow academy star Ethan Nwaneri could be sold for a combined £100m.

Gabriel Martinelli

Offloading Gabriel Martinelli may seem a ludicrous prospect, but rumours suggest the Gunners have their eyes on another world-class winger in the summer who can shine opposite Bukayo Saka.

‌



View 5 Images Martinelli has been linked with an exit (Image: Getty)

Martinelli has been a loyal servant to Arsenal and his pace off the bench has been key to their recent success. But his contract will end in 2027 unless the club exercises the option to extend it by an extra year. He is also far from the first name on the team sheet.

One would expect him to play at Selhurst Park, whether from the start or as a substitute, but if things materialise in the upcoming window, he might soon head elsewhere to play his football.

Article continues below

In January, Martinelli was linked with a move to the Saudi Pro League. More recent speculation claims that PSG and Bayern Munich are interested, with any sale potentially funding a blockbuster attacking arrival, along the lines of Julian Alvarez.

Sports.title: Casemiro's honest opinion on Man Utd transfer targets who could replace him
Sports.content:
Casemiro's honest opinion on Man Utd transfer targets who could replace him

Casemiro is set to leave Manchester United at the end of the season after four years at the club

View 3 Images Casemiro has been honest about who may replace him at Manchester United (Image: Gareth Copley/Getty Images)

Casemiro has big dreams for the future of Manchester United's midfield, having previously praised three of his potential successors. The Brazilian will leave Old Trafford following the final fixture of the season away to Brighton, bringing to a close a four-year spell with United.

‌



Casemiro arrived at the club following an extraordinarily successful stint with Real Madrid, claiming every available trophy in Spain. He established himself as one of the most respected defensive midfielders during his peak years, winning a remarkable five Champions Leagues with the La Liga side.

‌



But when his emotional exit from Madrid arrived, the 34-year-old expressed confidence that those inheriting his role in the centre of the pitch possessed the skills to fill the void. The three emerging talents charged with replacing the icon were Aurelien Tchouameni, Eduardo Camavinga and Federico Valverde.

‌



Now, this trio have been connected with transfers to United to assume Casemiro's position once again. Valverde is viewed as an outsider in Madrid following a training-ground confrontation with teammate Tchouameni.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Furious Roy Keane tears into Bruno Fernandes and Man Utd players' behaviour in wild rant READ MORE :

OPINION Abbie Meehan Man Utd can give Michael Carrick dream start by triggering £69m transfer release clause

‌



Reports indicate that club officials are enraged with the 27-year-old and may consider offloading him in the summer. Firm links between United and Valverde have yet to surface, and his asking price is expected to be substantial given his contract runs until 2029.

But Casemiro is convinced that the Uruguayan would suit the club following his earlier remarks about how gifted he was at a young age. Speaking after leaving Madrid in 2022, the Brazilian said: "Real Madrid always signs the best players. Fede can do this job, and he's a player with 10 or 12 years ahead of him.

View 3 Images Federico Valverde is potentially being ousted from Madrid (Image: Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images)

‌



"Four or five years ago, I was saying we had one of the best midfields in the world. Fede can play as a defensive midfielder."

Camavinga is another talent that Madrid are willing to entertain offers for, having featured less prominently in recent months. United have been associated with the France international, who has been omitted from his nation's World Cup squad.

He is accompanied by Tchouameni, who has been touted with a switch to Old Trafford in the summer. United's rivals Manchester City could prove crucial to this deal as Madrid are plotting a move for Rodri.

‌



The City midfielder has just over a year remaining on his contract at the Etihad and has previously acknowledged that "you can't turn down the best clubs in the world" when discussing a transfer to his homeland.

View 3 Images Eduardo Camavinga and Aurelien Tchouameni are also major targets (Image: David S. Bustamante/Soccrates/Getty Images)

Should Rodri move to the La Liga heavyweights, this could pave the way for United to secure Tchouameni's signature. Casemiro has previously praised the French pair as he insisted he was leaving the club "in good shape" for the future.

Article continues below

He added: "Camavinga showed us last year that he can be a fantastic player. Tchouameni is a player who is well-known at this club; he's a starter for the French national team. Real Madrid is in good shape and has good players."

All three United targets have earned the departing Casemiro's stamp of approval. However, any of the current Madrid stars would come with a substantial price tag, with a combined worth of £212m according to Transfermarkt.

Sports.title: Managing Arsenal as Mikel Arteta spends £255m on trio after winning Premier League title
Sports.content:
Managing Arsenal as Mikel Arteta spends £255m on trio after winning Premier League title

Arsenal will ride the wave of their success this season with another summer transfer spending spree

View 4 Images Mikel Arteta and Arsenal have an exciting summer ahead of them (Image: James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images)

A collective sigh of relief was let out across north London when the final whistle blew at the Vitality Stadium on Tuesday night, followed instantly by raucous celebrations in N5 and beyond. Arsenal are the deserved Premier League champions for the first time in 22 years.

‌



Naysayers will point at corner tactics and VAR but this has been a long time coming for a team that had only narrowly missed out for three consecutive seasons. The credit must go to the players for leaving everything on the pitch, the fans for their patience and, most of all, Mikel Arteta.

‌



Arsenal were in such disarray when the Spaniard took over as head coach six-and-a-half years ago that few could imagine such a day where they could break their Premier League drought and have a Champions League final still to look forward to.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

But the same principles that allowed Arteta to get to this stage will not allow him to rest on his laurels when all is said and done in Budapest later this month. He will almost immediately begin plotting and scheming for the summer and next season, if he hasn’t started already.

Now, Mirror Football predicts how the Gunners boss will build on this success and ensure his side dominates the Premier League for years to come.

‌



Arsenal confirm trophy parade details after Gunners win Premier League title READ MORE :

Record fee for Kroupi

It’s only right to sign the player who gifted Arsenal the title. Sentimental reasons aside, the 19-year-old Frenchman’s goal for Bournemouth against Manchester City showed exactly why so many teams are lining up to secure his signature, drifting into space before demonstrating incredible composure and technique with his finish.

Bournemouth recently stated they would not entertain offers of £85million for their talisman, who has scored 13 goals in his debut season in England. But even around £90m for Kroupi - a record sum by Arsenal for a forward - would be well worth it if the north Londoners manage to negotiate a fee with the Cherries.

View 4 Images Eli Junior Kroupi scored the goal to hand Arsenal the title (Image: Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

‌



He would add versatility along the front line, capable of playing as an inside forward from the left like Leandro Trossard or as a lone striker, as well as a much-needed goal threat. Kroupi also has the added bonus of being adored in north London before even putting on an Arsenal shirt.

Splurge on Barcola

Quality over quantity should be the main objective for Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta. Last year, the Gunners spent a record sum of over £250m on eight players.

Their needs have changed now to requiring more elite players rather than raising the floor of the entire squad. One such player that happens to be available on the market is Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola.

‌



Still just 23 years old, the Frenchman is world-class on counter-attacks and has more tools in his attacking arsenal than Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli. Barcola has grown frustrated at his lack of starts under Luis Enrique this term, given the Spaniard’s preference for Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue.

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola of PSG costs around £85m (Image: Getty Images)

Yet, he is needed at Arsenal, as seen by his heroics during last year’s treble-winning season, where he racked up a whopping 44 goal contributions in 64 appearances. Barcola is expected to cost a similar amount to Kroupi of just over £85m.

‌



Sell deadwood

It is understood that Arsenal have to sell players to spend heavily again this summer. Both Berta and predecessor Edu Gaspar have been underwhelming in past transfer windows when it comes to selling players for respectable sums.

It’s something the north Londoners still fall well behind their rivals in and an underrated part of transfer planning. Fortunately, there is no shortage of players set for the exit door this summer.

Gabriel Jesus, Christian Norgaard, Fabio Vieira, Ethan Nwaneri, Martinelli and Trossard could all be sold to make way for reinforcements. It is up to Berta to find suitors and negotiate deals that will help balance the books

‌



Shock Tonali move

View 4 Images Sandro Tonali is an elite midfielder (Image: Getty Images)

If, after signing Kroupi and Barcola, Arsenal still have money left in the account, Sandro Tonali of Newcastle would be a truly special acquisition. Until now, Arteta has been fortunate that Declan Rice has been ever-present. But he may not be injury-proof forever.

When that time comes, Arsenal need to be prepared. Tonali’s engine and duel-winning ability would make him both a seamless replacement for Rice and a potential midfield partner.

Article continues below

The Italian, 26, was heavily linked with a late move to Arsenal in January. His agent appears to be keen for him to move on too, especially with Newcastle set to miss out on European football.

Tonali is expected to cost upwards of £80m. Pulling off this signing, and the other two, will certainly not be easy. But such ambition is what separates title-winning teams from Premier League dynasties.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Shock Arne Slot sack instruction issued as Mohamed Salah 'makes U-turn'
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Shock Arne Slot sack instruction issued as Mohamed Salah 'makes U-turn'

The latest Liverpool news sees the Reds told to sack the under-fire Arne Slot as Mo Salah makes a call on his future

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah and Arne Slot haven't always be on the same page this season (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool look to have put one step in next season's Champions League after Manchester City took a point off Bournemouth on Tuesday evening. City's 1-1 draw with the Cherries means the Reds must avoid defeat to Brentford at Anfield on Sunday to secure a top-five finish.

‌



Even if Liverpool were to lose, Bournemouth would have to reverse a six-goal swing to overhaul the Reds. Barring a minor miracle, it appears the under-fire Arne Slot has found a relief at the end of the club's near-calamitous campaign.

‌



Tuesday night was symbolic for the Reds with City's draw also confirming Arsenal as champions, the north London club's first title in 22 years. The truth is, Liverpool meagrely surrendered the title they worked so tirelessly for last season to the Gunners months ago.

‌



Mikel Arteta's success will no doubt see the pressure on Slot continue. Today's news sees a former Liverpool star telling the club to sack the Dutch coach. Elsewhere, Mohamed Salah appears to have made a decision on his future.

Slot sack instruction

Liverpool must part ways with Slot, according to ex-Red Jermaine Pennant. Last Friday's 4-2 loss to Aston Villa means the Reds have lost 20 games across all competitions this season and Pennant thinks a change is urgently needed.

He said: "If the board thinks that this is the guy to stay in charge, then something's wrong with the board. Everyone can see this Liverpool team, see that they broke almost every single record which is not good - the most goals conceded, the most losses ever in a campaign, you name it. The stats are shocking."

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool owners told to BAN Mohamed Salah from final day send-off as behaviour addressed READ MORE :

Liverpool and Bournemouth could face dramatic play-off for Champions League spot READ MORE :

Pennant even backed up Salah, who slammed Liverpool's recent standards in a social media post last weekend. The former Arsenal star also claimed Liverpool cannot sanction another summer of lavish spending under the Dutchman.

"What he's saying [Salah] is stating the obvious. And if the board ultimately think that next season is going to be any different... I'm just shocked, because personally, I don't see how [things will change]," Pennant added.

‌



View 3 Images Arne Slot is under major pressure at Liverpool (Image: DARREN STAPLES, AFP via Getty Images)

"Are they going to spend another £450million, half a billion to bring in some more players? It's down to philosophy the way Liverpool play, how to play. They're playing like a mid-table team - they just sit back, they wait for teams to come onto them. There's no threat going forward, they're not aggressive.

"So you've built a great machine and then all of a sudden you change these same cogs in that machine and expect to get the right output. It's just not going to work."

‌



Mo Salah 'U-turn'

According to reports, Salah has given the "green light" to join Turkish giants Fenerbahce. The Reds forward dropped a bombshell statement in April that he would leave Anfield after nine trophy-laden years.

It was widely assumed that the winger would make a long-awaited move to the Saudi Pro League this summer, but if true the claims would suggest he's pulled off something of a U-turn on his future.

The Turkish outfit have reportedly made an "informal offer" to Salah of around £11m a year to keep the Egyptian icon in Europe. The report cautions that Salah has not "entirely ruled out" a move to Saudi Arabia, but he is targeting an ambitious project "at the highest level".

‌



View 3 Images Mohamed Salah is set to leave Liverpool at the end of the season (Image: Getty Images)

The reports echo Reds legend Jamie Carragher's thoughts earlier this season. He tipped Salah to snub Saudi Arabia for Europe. Speaking on Sky Sports, he said: "I think Mo Salah, the way he's driven like a Ronaldo, I don't see the Saudi thing just yet.

"I just think your career's over when you go there [Saudi Arabia]. I think he'll still be looking at his Champions League record or how many goals he can get.

Article continues below

"I still think he thinks, 'I'm still one of the best players, and me leaving now is not the end of my top-level career, I've still got something to give'."

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Barcelona manager intervenes in Rashford transfer as £100m bidding war emerges
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Barcelona manager intervenes in Rashford transfer as £100m bidding war emerges

Manchester United have an interesting summer transfer window in store as Marcus Rashford's situation at Barcelona takes a fresh twist

View 2 Images Hansi Flick has told Marcus Rashford he wants him at Barcelona next season (Image: Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Michael Carrick's first summer transfer window in charge at Manchester United looks set to be a manic one. The Old Trafford icon has already delivered his old team back to the Champions League but is now ready to be handed the reins in the market.

‌



Among the first orders of business for United will be to resolve Marcus Rashford's future. And the England forward has received a major update regarding his chances of competing a permanent move to Barcelona following a fruitful loan at the Camp Nou.

‌



There's also been a dramatic twist regarding the race for one Premier League star who could replace his compatriot. Mirror Football provides the latest news surrounding United in today's top headlines.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Flick wades into Rashford deal

The odds of Rashford joining Barca on a permanent deal appear to have improved after Hansi Flick green-lit the move. Reports in Spain suggest the German coach has informed Rashford he's counting on him returning to Catalonia once again.

Man Utd join Liverpool and Chelsea in race for Jarrod Bowen amid £100m West Ham fire sale READ MORE :

It recently came to light that Barcelona would prefer that to be in the form of another loan, with a view to making the move permanent in 2027. However, United are unwilling to accept those terms as they seek to sanction a sale this summer.

‌



Flick's assurance is a significant turn in the tale given it means he may apply pressure on Barcelona's board to complete a deal now. It's well-known La Liga's back-to-back champions aren't in the most financially secure position, but United will hope Robert Lewandowski's exit will free up the funds necessary to keep Rashford on board.

It's long been known that Barcelona can turn Rashford's move permanent for a fee of around £26million. The Spaniards have attempted to negotiate that figure down but United are standing firm on the figure for a player who has 14 goals and 14 assists this term.

In the event Flick doesn't get his man, United will presumably be happy to put Rashford in the shop window and potentially secure an even better sale figure. Meanwhile, Carrick would welcome the player back to Old Trafford in what could still be a major twist in the coming months.

‌

Bowen ignites £100m war

If Rashford does leave the club, one name in the frame to replace him will be West Ham's Jarrod Bowen. However, United will be far from the only Premier League powerhouse chasing his signature.

The Guardian reported West Ham will need to raise £100m from player sales this summer in the event they're relegated. And England ace Bowen will be one of the leading candidates to be sold in the event the east Londoners go down.

Bowen, 29, has eight goals and 10 assists so far this season ahead of Sunday's relegation decider at home to Leeds. Realistically, the Hammers need to beat Leeds and hope Spurs, who are currently two points ahead, lose at home to Everton to stand a chance of survival.

Article continues below

United may make a move for Bowen even if West Ham stay up given Nuno Espirito Santo's side will need to sell of talent regardless. It's believed the Red Devils are fans of Bowen's versatility in attack but the stiff competition for his signature could complicate matters.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta's private message revealed as star's price tag blocks transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta's private message revealed as star's price tag blocks transfer

Manager Mikel Arteta has helped guide Arsenal to Premier League glory

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has guided Arsenal to the Premier League title (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal are still savouring the feeling of being Premier League champions. The club’s 22-year wait ended on Tuesday, ensuring the title race did not go down to the final day.

‌



Mikel Arteta’s side rejoiced as Manchester City dropped points against Bournemouth to end their title challenge. The manager was not with his squad during their crowning moment but had put plans in place to ensure the team could celebrate their achievement together.

‌



It means that there will be no pressure on the Gunners’ final league match against Crystal Palace on Sunday. The trophy parade has been booked for May 31 and Arsenal fans will hope to see two pieces of silverware on display as the team look ahead to next week’s Champions League final.

‌



The Gunners will also have one eye on the upcoming transfer window, with one star reportedly open to leaving the club. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest Arsenal stories.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mikel Arteta's private message revealed

The Arsenal boss contacted his squad after their win against Burnley on Monday. Arteta sent a WhatsApp at 11pm to make sure that his players watched Manchester City’s clash with Bournemouth together at their London Colney training ground.

‌



Arsenal sent 'angry' message as Erling Haaland and Pep Guardiola speak their minds READ MORE :

The Spanish coach waited until his side had secured three points to share his message, not wanting his team to overlook their Burnley fixture. Once it was possible for the club to win the title on Tuesday night, Arteta delayed training until later in the day so that the squad could watch City’s game as a group.

Upon becoming champions, the Arsenal squad celebrated and were given permission to go out. Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Jurrien Timber and Eberechi Eze were pictured outside the Emirates Stadium at 5am.

The manager chose to watch the decisive match at home and spend the occasion with his family. However, he joined up with his players later that night.

‌



View 2 Images Ethan Nwaneri has been linked with Borussia Dortmund (Image: Franco Arland/Getty Images)

Arsenal star ‘open’ to move

Sky Sport Deutschland has reported that Borussia Dortmund are “making another attempt” to sign Ethan Nwaneri this summer. The Arsenal prospect has spent the second half of the season on loan at Marseille after struggling for minutes with the Gunners.

The German publication claims that Dortmund have asked about the 19-year-old’s situation. Nwaneri is reportedly “open” to joining the club this summer but a permanent move is deemed unlikely due to the “high transfer fee” required.

‌



The midfielder is under contract with the Gunners until 2030. Finalising a loan move is also claimed to be difficult for Dortmund, though the Bundesliga club remain interested in the Arsenal star.

Nwaneri has played in nine league games for Marseille, scoring twice. He had made six cameo appearances for Arsenal in the Premier League this season before heading to France.

Sports.title: Angry Southampton star breaks ranks after club kicked out of Championship play-off final
Sports.content:
Angry Southampton star breaks ranks after club kicked out of Championship play-off final

Southampton winger Leo Scienza has spoken of his "anger" and "sadness" after the club were denied the chance to play in the Championship play-off final due to Spygate

View 3 Images Leo Scienza has become the first Southampton player to comment (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

Southampton winger Leo Scienza has hinted at the chaos behind the scenes at the club after they were kicked out of the Championship play-off final for spying. Saints had appealed against the EFL punishment but discovered on Wednesday night that they had been unsuccessful.

‌



It means they will start the 2026/27 season on -4 points in the Championship, while Middlesbrough - the side they beat 2-1 in a two-legged play-off semi-final - will go to Wembley Stadium on Saturday to face Hull City.

‌



Saints manager Tonda Eckert is now facing the sack after it emerged that he was aware of the three spying trips the club admitted, to Oxford United, Ipswich and Middlesbrough. Meanwhile, the club are braced for more ramifications, with the FA likely to dish out further punishment, which could include a ban for those involved.

‌



It is understood that Southampton's players are considering their options after being robbed of a shot at promotion back to the Premier League by the actions of their own staff. And Scienza, who enjoyed an outstanding debut campaign for Saints, has become the first player to publicly voice his feelings on the subject.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Southampton LOSE Spygate appeal as Middlesbrough set for Championship play-off final READ MORE :

Southampton send desperate plea to their fans after being kicked out of play-off final READ MORE :

Scienza wrote on Instagram: "Disappointment, anger, sadness It's difficult to find the right words for what we're all feeling right now. What has happened over the last days is heartbreaking. for the club, for every player in this dressing room, and above all for our supporters. A moment like this should never end the way it did.

‌



"I feel sorry for every football fan, as well as the players and supporters of Hull and Boro, who were caught up in all of this chaos too.

"We gave everything for this dream. Day after day, sacrifice after sacrifice, always believing we could bring this club back to where it belongs. For me, the dream of playing in the Premier League was something I fought for with everything I had. That's why this pain cuts so deep.

View 3 Images Southampton were expelled despite beating Middlesbrough 2-1 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"The hardest part is knowing how much our fans deserved this moment. You stood behind us all season with incredible passion, loyalty and belief. Even in the toughest moments, you carried us forward. Thank you for staying with us through everything, you definitely deserved better."

Southampton's statement on Wednesday night read: "Southampton Football Club has this evening been informed that the EFL’s League Arbitration Panel has upheld the sanctions imposed earlier this week. As a result, the club will not participate in Saturday’s Championship Play-Off Final.

"This is an extremely disappointing outcome for everybody connected with Southampton Football Club. We know how painful this moment will be for our supporters, players, staff, commercial partners and the wider community who have given so much backing to the team throughout the season and we apologise once again to everyone impacted by this.

‌



View 3 Images Tonda Eckert now faces the consequences of Spygate (Image: Trevor Wilkinson/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"While we fully acknowledge the seriousness of this matter and the scrutiny that has followed, the club has consistently believed the original sporting sanction was disproportionate, a view that has been widely shared by many in the football community over the last 24 hours.

"We would like to place on record our sincere thanks to our supporters for the support, patience and loyalty they have shown throughout an incredibly difficult period. We will share information as soon as possible in relation to ticket refunds for those who bought tickets to Wembley.

‌



"Southampton Football Club has a proud history and strong foundations, but it is clear that trust now needs to be rebuilt. That work begins immediately. The club will reflect carefully on the events that have led to this point, learn from them and take the necessary steps to move forward responsibly.

"While tonight is a painful moment, this football club will respond with humility, accountability and determination to put things right."
